parallel.implementation: Subagents wrote the assigned files under /output/lib and /output/test12.mjs using BigInt, Map insertion order, Python repr formatting, and a root-collapse cutoff rule.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed the AgentSwarm result, executed /output/test12.mjs against the reference executable, and artifact validation collected test12.mjs plus four library modules.
parallel.verification: Children ran node --check and local smoke tests; parent ran CLI edge tests, help normalization, an 80-case targeted sweep, and the official evaluator passed 70/70.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No delivered correctness gap remained. A broad background sweep timed out and the cell process was marked timed out, but official evaluation still passed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual argparse, no external dependency, BigInt, and exact DeepDiff formatting requirements.

serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote pyrepr.mjs, deepdiff.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test12.mjs sequentially with a Map and BigInt approach matching the executable behavior.

serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No delivered correctness gap remained; an initial broader background sweep timed out but was replaced by a smaller completed sweep before final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized pure Node.js ESM, .mjs files, manual argparse parity, exact DeepDiff output formatting, no external dependencies, and black-box executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same ESM, CLI, output-format, dependency, and black-box probing requirements in a single actor flow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage gap; parallel delegated the same requirements to child-specific briefs, while serial kept them in one context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent split work into five subagents: pyint, pyrepr, argparse, deepdiff, and test12 entry, each with one assigned file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor performed probing, implementation, and verification itself without delegation or subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used explicit per-file ownership and then parent integration; serial used one continuous owner for all modules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The shared child prompt pinned exports, imports, .mjs suffixes, BigInt values, DeepDiff formats, cutoff rule, and assigned paths.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The single actor retained the reverse-engineered findings locally and implemented matching module interfaces directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an inter-agent contract boundary, but it was explicit and compatible; serial avoided the boundary by preserving context locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Subagents wrote /output/lib/pyint.mjs, pyrepr.mjs, argparse.mjs, deepdiff.mjs, and /output/test12.mjs, then the parent exercised the assembled entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The main serial actor wrote pyrepr.mjs, deepdiff.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test12.mjs sequentially and tested them.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented equivalent BigInt/Map-based DeepDiff emulation; file layout differed, with parallel using lib/ and serial placing modules at /output root.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All five subagents completed and their aggregate AgentSwarm result returned before parent verification began.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; the serial actor directly carried implementation outputs forward into verification and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join point at AgentSwarm completion, while serial had a simple local lifecycle; neither left required implementation results unjoined.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote to a shared /output tree but under distinct assigned paths, and parent tests ran the integrated /output/test12.mjs artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself under /output and verified them as a coherent program.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced shared workspace coordination but no collision or incompatible merge; serial avoided shared-write concurrency entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child syntax/smoke tests, parent argparse/help checks, an 80-case targeted differential sweep, and official evaluation passed 70/70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran executable probes, CLI edge cases, BigInt check, a 225 b-by-d differential sweep, and official evaluation passed 70/70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial completed its final local 225-case sweep before final response; parallel reported while an optional random sweep was still running, but both had enough verification for official pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five subagents and long background sweeps; one large sweep timed out and the cell marks the agent process timed out, but the artifact was already valid.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also launched an overly broad sweep that timed out once, then reduced it to a 225-case sweep that completed before final response; process_ok stayed true.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more lifecycle/budget noise and a timed-out outer process, while serial closed normally; this did not create an outcome difference because both official evaluations passed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: the current completed evaluations for both modes passed 70/70. The task-solving difference is procedural. Parallel used a parent-led probe, five module-specific subagents, an AgentSwarm join, and parent differential tests; serial performed the same probe-implement-verify loop in one actor and completed a smaller final sweep before closing. The parallel process timeout is observable but not a delivered-solution failure because artifact validation and official evaluation succeeded.
parallel_contributors: Useful parallel behavior: explicit module contracts let five subagents produce interoperable ESM files that the parent verified as an assembled program.
serial_contributors: Serial advantage: one actor preserved all reverse-engineered behavior in local context and completed a final 225-case sweep before the final answer.
ordinary_implementation_differences: File layout differed: parallel used /output/lib/*.mjs imports, while serial placed modules directly under /output; both layouts were acceptable to the evaluator.
evaluator_effects: No evaluator discrepancy observed; both current cell/status.json evaluation records are completed passes at 70/70.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process differences are comparative context rather than retained failure causes

candidates.reason: The parallel plan assigned every implementation module to a concrete child via AgentSwarm, and each child wrote its assigned file; implementation was not ownerless.
The parent kept integration responsibility through shared interface contracts and performed combined differential testing after the child files existed.
The entry deliverable was explicitly assigned to agent-4 and artifact validation found test12.mjs with required library files.
The parent owned the end-to-end pipeline from probing through delegation, collection, differential tests, and final report.
The parent did exploratory probing before delegation, but it did not block productive work behind an avoidable serial gate that left required implementation unfinished or unverified.
The exploratory phase produced usable DeepDiff and argparse rules, after which implementation and verification completed; there was no investigation-only phase causing incomplete delivery.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was starved; all required modules were written and accepted by the official evaluator.
The parallel run used five child agents and later long shell sweeps, but no required work was displaced by fan-out; the final artifact passed all 70 official cases.
Each child scope was a single file or entry point with clear bounds, and every child returned a completed artifact and syntax check.

Child briefs included ESM, .mjs, no external dependencies, BigInt arithmetic, exact interfaces, and file-specific behavior; no known requirement was omitted from a child in a way that made work unusable.
The AgentSwarm prompt pinned exports, imports, paths, value types, and DeepDiff formatting contracts, and the modules interoperated in parent tests.
No known finding disappeared in transfer: the parent provided the empirically derived cutoff and formatting rules in the shared prompt, and child summaries matched the assigned contracts.
Returned child handoffs were concise and used by the parent for integration testing; there is no evidence that report volume prevented consumption.
No child or parent acted on superseded workspace or requirement state; the only sibling-file observation confirmed files currently existed.
No incompatible child reports or contracts remained unresolved; child outputs described compatible module interfaces and the combined program passed tests.

The parent did present completion while an optional randomized sweep was still running, but it had already run targeted integrated differential tests and the task had no visible unresolved acceptance mismatch; official 70/70 later confirmed the artifact.
There was no replacement child or retry that restarted without inherited findings; later verification commands refined test coverage rather than repeating failed delegated work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child was explicitly stopped or cancelled before its needed work was finalized; all five subagents completed.
The deliverable and library files were already placed in /output before verification and final response; no complete candidate missed promotion before closure.
Parent-level integrated verification ran after the child writes and after the AgentSwarm result, not before the module implementations were merged.
The parent received the AgentSwarm result and then ran the assembled /output/test12.mjs against the reference executable, so delegated implementation was joined.
No verifier child produced a trapped finding; verification was performed by the parent through shell commands whose results were visible in the main trajectory.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; the only timed-out work was an oversized parent shell sweep after useful verification existed.
Completed child results were consumed: the parent inspected the AgentSwarm aggregate and proceeded to integrated differential testing based on the delivered files.
The parent checked the long sweep, reacted to timeout by running a targeted foreground sweep, and did not merely wait blindly for unavailable progress.
Children wrote distinct files under explicit module ownership; there were no competing designs claiming the same behavior that required unresolved reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source file; each child wrote a different assigned file.
No child replaced another child's non-entry source; write events show one owner per library module.
The entry file test12.mjs was written by its assigned child and later executed by the parent; no other actor overwrote that deliverable.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated provenance.
Although children shared /output, file ownership was isolated by path and produced no unstable-state or provenance problem.
A child observed sibling module files for optional smoke testing, but those were intended deliverables and no contamination or wrong reference state resulted.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The parallel long-sweep timeout is treated as budget noise rather than Load Imbalance, Blind Timeout Wait, or Unverified Global Completion because no required work/result was lost and both official evaluations passed.
